newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank leaves interest rates unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank leaves interest rates unchanged.

text.p: The Bundesbank said on Thursday its council left the German discount and Lombard rates unchanged after its regular meeting.

The German discount rate, the floor on interest rates, was left at 2.50 percent and the Lombard emergency financing rate, the ceiling on rates, at 4.50 percent. The central bank's main money market rate, the repo, was also kept steady at a fixed rate of three percent.

Few economists had expected the Bundesbank to take action on the headline rates, held steady since April 1996, since economic data on Wednesday showed modest growth and minimal inflation and supported the case for stable interest rates.

Growth in M3 money supply, the Bundesbank's top indicator, which had surged to an alarming 11.7 percent in January, slowed to 9.1 percent in February as strong bond markets tempted investors to move funds into long-term investments.

The closely-watched west German Ifo business climate index also edged up to 93.6 in February from 93.3 the previous month, providing more evidence that the gloom that has long plagued the German corporate world was slowly lifting.

And as Germany battles with record post-World War Two unemployment, growth is still seen as far too restrained to sustain a rate increase. On the other, money supply growth remains too robust to justify easing rates, economists said.
